Inspection of ignition leads should include both a visual and an electrical test [1].

**Visual Inspection:**
*   Inspect the lead cover for cracks or other damage, abrasions, mutilated braid, or other physical damage [1].
*   Inspect leads for overheating if they are routed close to exhaust stacks [1].
*   Inspect connectors for damaged threads, corrosion, cracked insulators, and bent or broken connector pins [2].
*   Inspect leads for worn or burned areas, deep cuts, fraying, and general deterioration [2].
*   Inspect the contact springs and compression springs for any damage or distortion [1].
*   Inspect the sleeves for cracks or carbon tracking [1].
*   Inspect the coupling nut that connects to the spark plug for damaged threads or other defects [1].

**Electrical Inspection:**
*   Perform a continuity check of ignition leads [2].
*   Check each lead for continuity using a high-tension lead tester by connecting the black lead to the contact spring and the red lead to the eyelet of the same lead in the cover; the continuity lamp on the tester should illuminate when tested [1].
*   Perform an insulation resistance test using the high-tension lead tester by attaching the red (high-voltage) lead to the spring of the harness lead and the black lead to the ferrule of the same lead [1].
*   Depress the press-to-test push button switch on the lead tester and observe that the indicator lamp flashes and the gap fires simultaneously as long as the switch is held in the depressed position [1].
*   If the indicator lamp flashes and the gap fails to fire, the lead under test is defective and must be replaced [1].
